events.title: King John Agrees to Magna Carta Negotiations at Runnymede
events.description: Rebel barons and King John of England began the final negotiations at Runnymede that led to the sealing of the Magna Carta, with the charter issued on June 15 and formalized in the days after. The document limited royal authority and affirmed that the king was subject to the law.
events.significance: The Magna Carta became a foundational document in the development of constitutional government and the rule of law in England and beyond.

events.title: Continental Congress Adopts the Stars and Stripes
events.description: The Second Continental Congress passed the Flag Resolution, stipulating that the flag of the United States have thirteen alternating red and white stripes and thirteen white stars on a blue field.
events.significance: The resolution established the original national flag of the United States, a lasting symbol of the nation, and is commemorated annually as Flag Day.

events.title: German Troops Enter Paris
events.description: During World War II, German forces occupied Paris without resistance after the French government had declared it an open city and withdrawn. The occupation lasted until the city's liberation in August 1944.
events.significance: The fall of Paris was a decisive moment in the Battle of France and led to the French armistice, reshaping the course of World War II in Western Europe.

events.title: Birth of Donald Trump
events.description: Donald John Trump was born in Queens, New York City. He became a real estate developer and television personality before being elected the 45th President of the United States in 2016 and the 47th in 2024.
events.significance: Trump became a highly influential and polarizing figure in modern American politics, and one of only a few presidents to serve non-consecutive terms.

events.title: Mariner 5 Launched Toward Venus
events.description: NASA launched the Mariner 5 space probe, which flew by Venus in October 1967 and gathered data on the planet's atmosphere, magnetic field, and radiation environment.
events.significance: Its measurements revealed that Venus has a very dense, hot atmosphere, greatly improving understanding of planetary science.
